findings.candidateCauseGroup: bilateral knee-demonstration contour protrusion; endpoint/weight field, knee pivot/pose mapping, source mesh or preparation interpolation remain alternatives, not selected causes
findings.phase: preparation (clip 2.25 s of 3.0 s in capture index), intermediate 1.5 s, peak 3.0 s, return 1.5 s; dense keyframe and adjacent-midpoint sheets
findings.reproduction: In frozen emitted-GLB full-cycle playback, use rate=0.25 and seek to headers 11/74 (left) and 18/74 (right); compare dense v3 sheets groups 11 and 18. Existing learner screenshots show the preparation/action/reset flow; re-open the two knee action source routes and use the existing demonstration.
findings.expectedAppearance: Rectus femoris surface stays attached at proximal/distal boundaries and follows knee extension, without a detached arc or excessive outward bulge; returns to rest.
findings.actualObservation: Smooth outward contour without a visible tear or clear pop. The preparation/peak protrusion cannot be classified as expected shape change versus excessive protrusion at this evidence scale.
findings.nextAction: MV2 Sol: diagnose only if selected as the one fixed common-cause group; compare left/right source transform, endpoint weights, pivot, preparation mapping and adjacent interpolation before editing.

findings.candidateCauseGroup: lateral surface overlap/occlusion versus actual penetration or local mesh-fit; lighting/view depth ambiguity also possible
findings.phase: action and return across dense keyframe/midpoint samples; full cycle group 9
findings.reproduction: Open frozen playback-v3 full-cycle, rate=0.25; locate 9/74 External abdominal oblique muscle · left · T66-PRIORITY-S04-FLEX. Compare frontal, lateral and oblique rows in dense group 9 and the frozen focused-phase sheet.
findings.expectedAppearance: Highlighted oblique remains continuous and attached while changing shape; nearby structures do not intersect or separate over the cycle.
findings.actualObservation: The highlighted target remains continuous and returns; lateral view has a persistent layered/jagged pale contour behind it. No abrupt temporal pop was confirmed, but overlap versus penetration cannot be decided from the overview.
findings.nextAction: MV2 Sol: inspect source frame, depth ordering and exact neighboring surface pair before treating this as a geometric defect.

findings.candidateCauseGroup: lateral dark layer / selected-target visibility and source-surface overlap under elbow and shoulder motion
findings.phase: elbow-flexion action/return and shoulder-flexion action/mid/return; groups 21–24
findings.reproduction: Use rate=0.25 in the frozen full-cycle player; select 21/74 left elbow flexion, then 23/74 left and 24/74 right shoulder flexion. Compare v3 dense sheets and focused-phase sheets for groups 21–24.
findings.expectedAppearance: Selected biceps surface follows the intended joint motion with stable attachments and readable separation from neighboring layers through action and reset.
findings.actualObservation: No clear tear or temporal pop in the observed frames. The lateral dark region and small target effect make overlap/contact and attachment quality inconclusive; no normality inferred.
findings.nextAction: MV2 Sol: compare matching left/right clips and member-role transforms; determine whether the dark lateral layer is expected neighboring context or a contact/weight issue.

findings.candidateCauseGroup: small distal joint excursion and target-specific surface deformation may be below whole-scene legibility, or hidden by layered hand geometry; do not infer absent motion or normal contraction
findings.phase: rest, preparation, intermediate, peak and return; groups 45–70; dense keyframe and adjacent-midpoint views
findings.reproduction: For each of the 26 exact mappings below, select the listed learner action, turn on selected emphasis, use the existing playback control, slow the corresponding emitted-GLB segment to 0.25x, and compare target motion with the adjacent joint and return. Retain the selected-target crop/scale used by the original review sheets.
findings.expectedAppearance: The associated distal muscle surface follows its named finger/thumb joint action and returns, with movement visible enough to understand the selected target; this is a qualitative expectation, not a numeric amplitude threshold.
findings.actualObservation: The actions and reset are reachable and operable in the learner UI. In whole-limb overview sheets many local finger changes are subtle or hard to distinguish; no gross temporal tear was confirmed. Target-specific naturalness remains unresolved.
findings.nextAction: MV2 Sol: choose one fixed common-cause cluster only after checking whether the same authoring/transform pattern is shared; separate scale/readability from mesh deformation.
